C-SEC-AUDIT-FIXES.Summary: Remediation of the six findings of the 2026-11-09 security audit (F-001..F-006), all re-verified statically against main 9b054d4d, in three waves: release supply-chain pinning (F-004), extension IPC hardening (F-002, F-003, F-005), and local path/link hardening (F-001, F-006). One change because the findings share the same verification shape — isolated negative-case proofs mirroring the audit's check boxes — and ride one release train (2.9.x-next).
C-SEC-AUDIT-FIXES.Problem: (F-004) The release job build (environment release-signing, permissions id-token: write and attestations: write) runs tools/verify-attributions.sh:31 `npx --yes --package license-checker` (no version pin at all) and release.yml:486 `npx --yes --package @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm@6.0.1`; neither package exists in package.json or package-lock.json, so every release resolves fresh code from the npm registry — in contrast to the neighboring cargo tools, which are pinned `--version --locked` (release.yml:466, release.yml:478). tools/stats-gateway/README.md:183 additionally documents an unpinned `npx wrangler deploy` pattern. (F-002) POST /ext/text-insert (live_server.rs:917) accepts only State and Json — its own comment says "No auth required" — attributes the request to a hardcoded extension id (com.tokmo.voice) and emits mt::text::op into the active editor; the route is registered unconditionally (live_server.rs:1215) and the server runs in every non-MAS desktop build (main.rs:779). (F-003) mt_ext_disable flips only registry.enabled; incoming /ext/context (live_server.rs:967) and /ext/apply (live_server.rs:1045) authenticate via validate_bearer_extension (live_server.rs:407), which checks stored-token validity only and never consults ExtRegistry, and the pairing secret is not revoked on disable. (F-005) validate_manifest (manifest.rs:160-195) extracts the base_url host by string split on ':' then '/'; a manifest base_url like http://localhost:1@evil.example/ passes the loopback check because the split sees "localhost", while the real network recipient sits after the userinfo '@'; invoke_extension then attaches the bearer secret and payload without re-validating the final URL. (F-001) mt_format_link_click (m_v1_compat.rs:868-903) joins a relative href with the document dirname and passes the result to opener open_path with neither m010 check_path nor check_shell_open_extension nor check_url_scheme — a Ctrl/Cmd+click on a planted relative link can hand a sibling .command/.app to the OS handler. (F-006) check_path (m010_security.rs:231) resolves symlinks only when the requested path already exists; for a not-yet-created file whose existing parent is a symlink pointing outside the workspace, only the lexical prefix is checked, and fs_write_inner (m013b/fs.rs:122-125) then runs create_dir_all plus File::create outside the sandbox — the same control covers binary writes and directory creation.

Goals.Goal: Wave 1 — The release job resolves zero npm packages outside the committed lockfile: license-checker and @cyclonedx/cyclonedx-npm become pinned devDependencies installed by the existing npm ci and are invoked as local binaries; a repository guard fails if a fresh-resolving `npx --yes` reappears in release.yml; the documented wrangler deploy snippet in tools/stats-gateway/README.md is pinned or removed.

Wave 2 — Every incoming /ext/* route requires a valid bearer token for a real, enabled extension holding the matching capability: /ext/text-insert loses its no-auth status and hardcoded identity; /ext/context and /ext/apply check ExtRegistry.enabled in addition to token validity.

Wave 2 — Disabling an extension ends its incoming access at that moment: mt_ext_disable revokes the stored pairing secret (auth::revoke_secret), previously issued tokens stop authenticating, and re-enabling requires a new pairing.

Wave 2 — Extension base_url validation parses with a real URL parser (the url crate, already in Cargo.lock), rejects userinfo and non-loopback parsed hosts including bracketed IPv6 forms, and the outgoing invoke re-validates the final URL before attaching the bearer; redirects to a different recipient are refused.

Wave 3 — mt_format_link_click validates before opening: http(s) links are unchanged; local and relative targets pass check_path against the document workspace and check_shell_open_extension, dangerous executable targets are refused with a log marker, and ordinary document/image links keep opening.

Wave 3 — check_path resolves the nearest existing ancestor when the requested path does not exist yet and requires the canonicalized ancestor to stay inside the sandbox, closing the parent-symlink escape for new text files, binary writes, and directory creation, while preserving the Windows permissive-root and drive-prefix behavior of C-WINDOWS-SAVE-PIPELINE.

Constraints.Constraint: The audit's preserved-user-scenario rule: relative links to ordinary documents and images still open, an enabled paired extension keeps working across the hardened routes, and an inward-pointing symlink still saves — every hardening ships with its legitimate-path proof.
No new entitlements and no listener-surface changes: the live server stays on 127.0.0.1 with an OS-assigned port and the MAS build keeps its no-listener status.
Prefer zero new user-visible strings (log markers and IPC errors only); any refusal notice that does become user-visible follows the ten-locale rule.
Release-pipeline hardening follows the existing cargo-tool pattern (pinned version, lockfile-resolved, warm-cache friendly) and must not add material wall-clock cost to the release job.

The tools/stats-gateway/README.md leg of wave 1 does not race the approved C-STATS-DASH-PUSH and C-STATS-READOUT changes (both ready-to-execute, both rewriting README sections inside M-071, already overlapping each other there): wave 1 touches that file only after those changes are archived, or under an explicit hand-off recorded in the plan — M-071 and V-M-071 stay declared as adjacent anchors in AffectedAreas (the overlapped module's verification anchor at spec level; the plan's VerificationAnchors declares the full per-module set) so the overlap remains visible to grace.
The link-click fix reuses the existing m010 checks; no parallel hand-rolled validation policy is introduced.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Redesigning the extension pairing UX; the pre-existing native-approval-dialog TODO in handle_pair stays untouched.
A runtime confirmation dialog for executable link targets — this change hard-blocks per the existing shell-open policy; the dialog option is recorded as a deferred decision in the design context.
Descriptor-based (openat-style) sandbox-proof writes; nearest-existing-ancestor resolution is the accepted scope for F-006.
Changing muya link sanitization — relative links stay renderable by design; only the open path is hardened.
Findings or threat modeling beyond F-001..F-006; the audit's not-established premises (remote reachability, browser-origin requests, OS launch outcomes) remain out of scope.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: F-004: the attribution and SBOM steps of the release job execute lockfile-installed local binaries with zero fresh registry resolution (verifiable from workflow logs and by removing network access), a repository guard fails on fresh-resolving npx patterns in release.yml, and tools/stats-gateway/README.md contains no unpinned npx instruction.

F-002: a /ext/text-insert request without a valid bearer for an enabled extension holding the text-insert capability returns 401/403 and emits no mt::text::op event, while the authorized paired flow still inserts text — proven by live-server tests.
F-003: after mt_ext_disable, previously valid tokens are refused on /ext/context and /ext/apply and the stored secret is revoked; a fresh pairing restores access — proven by tests.

F-005: parser unit tests with no network calls reject userinfo URLs (http://localhost:1@evil.example/), non-loopback parsed hosts, and cross-recipient redirects, while well-formed loopback manifests (127.0.0.1, localhost, ::1) still validate.

F-001: unit tests around the link-click validation path prove that a relative link to a .command/.app (any DANGEROUS_SHELL_OPEN_EXTENSIONS entry) is refused with a log marker and nothing reaches the opener, that a relative .md/.png inside the workspace still opens, and that http(s) handling is unchanged.

F-006: writing a new text file, writing a new binary file, and creating a directory through a parent symlink that points outside the workspace are all rejected; the same symlink pointing inward still works; overwrite of an existing outside file via symlink stays rejected (regression); the Windows permissive-root suite stays green.

Process: grace lint --change C-SEC-AUDIT-FIXES --assertions target passes during implementation, --assertions final --run-commands passes before archiving, and the change introduces zero new graph integrity errors.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: cargo test --bin mark --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml (m010, m013, m045 and v1-compat suites); npm test (affected renderer/IPC suites); the release-workflow no-fresh-resolution guard; grace lint --path . --change C-SEC-AUDIT-FIXES --assertions target during implementation and --assertions final --run-commands before archiving.
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: One green negative-case test per audit check box (six findings, each with its preserved-legitimate-path companion test); existing suites stay green; release CI logs show lockfile-installed binaries; grace lint reports zero errors attributable to this change's files.

Assumptions.Assumption: All six findings were re-verified statically on 2026-11-09 against main 9b054d4d and every cited line matched; no dynamic exploitation was attempted, and the audit's per-finding check boxes are adopted verbatim as this change's acceptance criteria.
The url crate (2.5.8) is already present in Cargo.lock as a transitive dependency; promoting it to a direct dependency of the workspace crate adds no new vendor code.

AffectedAreas routing (corrected after gate pass 1 of 2026-11-09): M-010 (m010_security.rs), M-045 (m045_ext/), M-054 and M-046 (.github/workflows/release.yml, tools/release-*, package.json, package-lock.json) are confirmed owners; m_v1_compat.rs appears verbatim in the PlannedPaths of M-033 and M-069, so both are declared and the plan confirms the routing owner (M-033 is the semantic owner of the v1 IPC surface; M-069 shares the path); tools/stats-gateway/README.md is owned by M-071 and declared with the sequencing constraint above; m013b/fs.rs appears in no graph path (grep-verified) and M-002 stays its provisional owner until the plan settles or reroutes it.
The stats-gateway wrangler snippet may be fully obsolete (the CF-token route was cancelled by the owner on 2026-11-03); wave 1 updates or removes it accordingly rather than pinning dead instructions.
The extension live server ships in production desktop builds today (main.rs cfg not(feature = "app-store")); no feature flag shields the wave-2 routes.
